First float? Here's the lay of the river.

The Puntledge runs from Comox Lake down into Courtenay. Tubers stick to the lower, mellow half. Everything upstream of the marked put-ins belongs to the dam, the falls, and the expert kayakers.

Save this map

Reception on the river is spotty. Keep a copy downloaded.

For orientation, not navigation. Markers are approximate, so scout your put-in and take-out from shore before you launch. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.

Sirens along the river mean water is rising: exit the channel immediately.

BC Hydro releases water from the Comox Dam without public notice. Never float upstream of the diversion dam or anywhere near Nymph Falls, Barber's Hole, or the powerhouse.

Pick your float

All three floats put in at the Puntledge River Hatchery. Park along Watts Rd near the trailhead. Get directions to the put-in

Liveliest water

Hatchery → Puntledge Park

30–45 min Fast, bumpy channels

The top of the run is the liveliest water: quick, braided channels with little wave trains and bumps to bounce through before the river settles down. The shortest float, out at Puntledge Park, and the one to pick if you want the playful part without the long lazy tail.

Most popular

Hatchery → Condensory Bridge

45–75 min The classic run

The run most tubers actually do: the lively water up top, then a mellow cruise down to Condensory Bridge. Get out here. Below the bridge the current fades and the float turns into a hand-paddle slog, more so on an incoming tide.

The long haul

Hatchery → Lewis Park

75–120 min Lazy tidal finish

Float all the way into Courtenay. Lewis Park is the LAST exit before the estuary. Everything past Condensory slows right down, and the final leg is tidal, so an incoming tide means real paddling. Check tide times first.

How a float day works

1

Check conditions first

Look at today’s report, the dam-release note, and the weather before anyone gets in a car.
2

Set your shuttle

Leave a car, a bike, or a patient friend at your exit: Puntledge Park, Condensory Bridge, or Lewis Park. Floating past it means a long, soggy walk back.
3

Park and launch

At the hatchery, park along Watts Rd near the trailhead. Wherever you stop, obey the posted signs: don’t block driveways, farm gates, or emergency routes, and launch from the gravel bars, not private banks. Some lots are gated and lock at set times (Lewis Park included), and we don’t track those hours. Tickets, tows, and break-ins all happen, so take your valuables with you.
4

Don’t miss your exit

Know what your take-out looks like before you launch: scout it from shore when you drop the shuttle. Miss it and your last chance is Lewis Park. After that it’s tidal estuary, and an incoming tide will fight you the whole way.
5

Tell other tubers

Take a few seconds to report your float: water level, crowds, anything weird. That’s what keeps this site useful.

What to bring (and bring back)

Life jacket (PFD)Water shoesSun shirt + hatNon-nano mineral sunscreenWater bottleDry bag for phone + keysPatch kit or spare tubeGarbage bag for wrappers

Sunscreen washes off in the river, and chemical UV filters such as oxybenzone can harm fish. A sun shirt means less to wash off; for the rest, non-nano zinc oxide or titanium dioxide is the option with the least evidence of harm.

Please make sure whatever goes in with you, comes out with you. There are garbage and recycling bins at Puntledge Park and Lewis Park.

Check today's conditions before you drive out. The river changes day to day.
